# octopusdeploy_service_account_oidc_identity (Resource)

This resource manages manages OIDC service account for the associated user

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "octopusdeploy_user" "github_actions" {
  display_name  = "GitHub Actions"
  email_address = "github-actions@example.com"
  is_active     = true
  is_service    = true
  username      = "github-actions"
}

resource "octopusdeploy_service_account_oidc_identity" "github_actions" {
  name               = "GitHub Actions main branch"
  service_account_id = octopusdeploy_user.github_actions.id
  issuer             = "https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com"
  subject            = "repo:my-org/my-repo:*"

  # The token must pass every condition. Each condition passes when the claim matches any one of its values.
  # Leave this out to keep the existing conditions. Set it to [] to remove them all.
  claim_conditions = [
    {
      claim  = "repository_owner"
      values = ["my-org"]
    },
    {
      claim  = "ref"
      values = ["refs/heads/main", "refs/tags/v*"]
    },
  ]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `issuer` (String) OIDC issuer url
- `name` (String) The name of this resource.
- `service_account_id` (String) ID of the user to associate this identity to
- `subject` (String) OIDC subject claims

### Optional

- `audience` (String) OIDC audience
- `claim_conditions` (Attributes List) Extra conditions the token's claims must pass before Octopus exchanges the token for an access token. The token must pass every condition. When you leave this out, Terraform keeps the conditions that are already on the identity. Set it to `[]` to remove every condition. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--claim_conditions))

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The unique ID for this resource.

<a id="nestedatt--claim_conditions"></a>
### Nested Schema for `claim_conditions`

Required:

- `claim` (String) The name of the token claim to check.
- `values` (List of String) The values the claim can match. The claim passes when it matches any one value. Values use the same matching rules as the subject: `*` matches any sequence of characters and `?` matches one character. Matching is case sensitive. A value made only of `*` characters is rejected.
